close_reason: Fixed in same commit as JMAP-tjvm.7. New crate-jmap-mail-client/tests/extras_passthrough_tests.rs file holds 6 wire-level tests (1 per method that accepts a *Params struct with extras): each constructs the params with a vendor key in 'extra', invokes the production method through SessionClient, and asserts the vendor key appears at the correct path in args under server.received_requests()[0]. The struct-level tests in src/methods/mod.rs remain — they verify the serde derive contract; the new tests verify the production-method wire-passthrough contract. Both layers are needed; one tests serde, the other tests the method.
description:
The 9 extras-policy tests in src/methods/mod.rs (lines 714-839) all follow
the same shape:
```rust
let params = SomeParams { extra: {acme: ...}, ... };
let v = serde_json::to_value(&params).unwrap();
assert_eq!(v["acmeCorpFoo"], json!(...));
```
These test that the *struct* serializes its extras correctly. They do NOT
test that the production method (`email_get`, `email_copy`, etc.) actually
includes those extras in the JMAP request body that goes onto the wire.

This is why bd:JMAP-tjvm.7 (silent-drop in email_copy, mailbox_set,
email_submission_set) was not caught by the test suite: the struct serializes
perfectly, but the production method discards the result.

Fix: replace each per-struct extras test with a wiremock smoke test that:
  1. constructs the params with a vendor key in extras,
  2. calls the production method through SessionClient,
  3. inspects server.received_requests()[0] and asserts the vendor key is in
     methodCalls[0][1] (the args).

This exercises the same code path callers do. The struct-level test is
necessary but not sufficient.

This applies to every extension-client sibling cookie-cut from this template.
title: extras round-trip tests verify struct serialization, not wire passthrough
